title: Occasional crashes in nightlies when unlocking laptop
body: I'm using WezTerm nightly 20230108-184945-d34297cd on macOS 13.1 with no config. For the last few weeks, WezTerm has occasionally disappeared shortly after I wake and unlock my MacBook, sometimes before the desktop is visible. It happens about once every two or three days and has not happened while I am actively using the machine. I don't have reliable reproduction steps. The latest macOS crash log reports EXC_BAD_ACCESS on the main thread and includes window::os::macos::menu::Menu::items in the stack.

symptoms_visible: WezTerm occasionally disappears shortly after I wake and unlock my MacBook, sometimes before the desktop is visible.
The crash happens about once every two or three days and has not happened while I am actively using WezTerm.
The macOS crash report records EXC_BAD_ACCESS on the main thread and lists window::os::macos::menu::Menu::items in the stack.
N0.label: N0 sporadic post-unlock crash reported

symptoms_visible: A couple of minutes after unlocking, WezTerm was initially responsive but became frozen when I focused one of its windows after using Safari.
Under lldb, the main thread stopped with EXC_BAD_ACCESS in objc_msgSend called from AppKit routeKeyEquivalent.
N1.label: N1 debug crash captured

symptoms_visible: WezTerm crashed while I manually changed the system appearance from dark to light without pressing a hotkey.
After repeating the appearance toggle, I can bring on the crash, including when WezTerm is using the default config.
N2.label: N2 appearance-change trigger found

symptoms_visible: Pressing Command-R for the fifth config reload consistently crashes my debug build, even if I type, manipulate splits, or focus other windows between reloads.
N3.label: N3 deterministic reload reproduction

symptoms_visible: After updating and rebuilding, I can repeatedly reload the config without WezTerm crashing.
N4.label: N4 candidate update verified

symptoms_visible: Repeated config reloads no longer crash WezTerm on a build containing the correction.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: How many WezTerm windows, tabs, and splits are normally open when this happens?
Do you typically have multiple WezTerm windows open at the time of the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I generally have two or three WezTerm windows open, each with a few tabs, and most tabs have at least one split.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I normally have only one window and one tab open.

question_patterns: Do you run any third-party hotkey, shortcut, menu, or bundle-injection utilities?
Are there utilities installed that may modify menus or inject code into applications?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I do not run any utilities that I'm aware of that should inject code into running apps.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, the crashes only happen while a third-party menu utility that injects into applications is enabled.

question_patterns: Could you build from a full git clone with release debug symbols enabled and run that build for a few days?
Can you attach lldb, continue the process, and capture bt all when the problem occurs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm running the debug build under lldb. I left it attached until the next failure and captured the full stack trace.

question_patterns: What does the full lldb backtrace show when the debug build fails?
Please paste the raw bt all output from the next crash.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A couple of minutes after unlocking, WezTerm was responsive at first, then froze when I focused it after looking at Safari. The lldb trace stops with EXC_BAD_ACCESS in objc_msgSend, called by AppKit routeKeyEquivalent and then NSApplication sendEvent:.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The backtrace shows the crash entirely in the terminal's renderer worker thread, with no AppKit event or menu-related frames.
The same AppKit routeKeyEquivalent stack was captured after a longer delay following unlock.

edges.comment: Reporter chain from c2, c4, c16: jason0x43 described the multi-window setup and lack of injection utilities, ran a locally built debug-symbol bundle, attached lldb, and supplied the raw crash stack. CoralPink's logout behavior and artifacts are a separate deployment and are deliberately excluded.

question_patterns: Do you remember whether you used a keyboard shortcut immediately before the crash?
What input or interaction occurred just before the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not sure whether I used a shortcut before that crash. If I did, it most likely would have been Command-N or Command-T; I use custom bindings for most other interactions.

question_patterns: Can you watch for the exact interaction immediately preceding the next crash?
If it happens again under lldb, what were you doing at that moment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The next crash happened right when I manually toggled the system appearance from dark to light, and I hadn't pressed any hotkeys. After trying it repeatedly, toggling the appearance definitely brings on a crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Appearance changes never reproduce it; every captured crash instead follows the same custom key binding.
It reproduces when switching from light to dark rather than dark to light.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c17-c25: jason0x43 was initially unsure about shortcut use, then captured crashes during manual appearance changes with no hotkey and volunteered that the same behavior occurs with the default configuration.

question_patterns: Can you try repeatedly reloading the configuration and report exactly what happens?
Does performing several config reloads provide a reliable reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For me it has happened 100% of the time on the fifth Command-R config reload. The reloads can be consecutive or separated by typing, creating and removing splits, and focusing other windows; when I return and perform the fifth reload, WezTerm crashes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I reloaded the config dozens of times in the same debug build and could not reproduce the crash.
It consistently crashes after the fourth reload rather than the fifth.

edges.comment: Reporter measurement from c26-c29: after wez mentioned a rapid reload reproduction, jason0x43 tested the behavior and reported the raw, highly consistent fifth-reload outcome on the reporter's debug build.

question_patterns: Could you update to the latest source, rebuild, and repeat the same config-reload reproduction?
Please test the updated build with repeated Command-R reloads and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: That update appears to resolve it for me. Repeatedly reloading the config no longer crashes WezTerm.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated build still crashes consistently on the fifth config reload.
The updated build survived twenty reloads instead of the smaller repeated-reload test.

edges.comment: Pre-resolution build verification from c27-c30 on jason0x43's system. The reporter states only the observed result after updating and rebuilding; the reference-count diagnosis remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct ownership of the macOS application's main-menu reference so repeated config reloads and appearance-triggered menu rebuilds do not over-release it and later send messages to a stale menu object.
solution.concrete_example: Adjust the macOS main-menu handling so WezTerm does not treat the returned menu reference as an owned reference and release it after each rebuild. Ship that correction in a nightly after confirming that the reporter's formerly deterministic repeated-reload test no longer crashes.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw crash stacks and reproduction results. The maintainer inferred that appearance changes reload the config and rebuild or adjust the menu, then identified the ownership error: WezTerm incorrectly believed it owned the main-menu reference and released it after use, decrementing the internal reference count until NSApp could return a stale or freed menu object.

edges.comment: Accepted diagnosis and resolution from c26-c32: wez connected appearance changes to config reload and menu adjustment, reproduced the crash through repeated reloads, corrected the main-menu reference-count handling, and jason0x43 verified the updated build with the deterministic reload test.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: incorrect ownership and reference counting of the macOS main-menu object caused repeated config reloads or menu adjustments to over-release it, eventually leaving AppKit with a stale or freed menu reference.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the debug lldb stack, the appearance-change trigger, and the deterministic repeated-config-reload reproduction rather than inferred from the original sporadic post-unlock symptom alone.

Must not blame the crash on the reporter's custom configuration or require a specific menu shortcut as the trigger: it reproduced with the default config and during appearance changes without a hotkey.
The corrective action must fix main-menu reference ownership and avoid the erroneous release, not merely advise reducing the number of windows or avoiding config reloads.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies that repeated config reloads no longer crash a build containing the correction.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient macOS user and developer: can build a Rust project from a git clone, enable debug symbols, run WezTerm under lldb, inspect stack traces, and perform controlled reproduction tests.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, concise, and analytical with light humor; volunteers precise observations, distinguishes correlation from direct cause, and carefully retests hypotheses.
